Implementation slice of the accepted backend-neutral direction tracked in [pm-cli #1399](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1399). Specific backend-interface designs below remain proposals pending the shared core contract; this is roadmap work, not a claim of a shipped defect.

**Goal / scope.** Shared SDK semantics should support a native backend without weakening Azure-specific revisions, mappings and recovery. Feed these requirements into the upstream contract before treating a SQL CRUD adapter as sufficient.

**Static evidence at 7f44a1d.** The adapter already has `PmClient` reconciliation, but [resolution's authoritative document read](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/blob/7f44a1dbd19ef2c9808c96944b34c41e890ebbcd/resolution.ts#L180-L201) additionally calls `readSettings`, `locateItem` and `readLocatedItem` with `pmRoot`. [Settlement detection](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/blob/7f44a1dbd19ef2c9808c96944b34c41e890ebbcd/resolution.ts#L252-L257) resolves a filesystem history path. The apply flow also depends on mutation previews, durable intent and fenced local mutation callbacks. These are SDK APIs, not ad hoc raw storage writes, but remain path-bound and expose the contract surface a backend must replace.

**Existing work / nonduplication.** Build on [revision-bound conflict resolution PR #41](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/pull/41) and [its canonical acceptance record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/blob/7f44a1dbd19ef2c9808c96944b34c41e890ebbcd/.agents/pm/features/pm-ado-4x3u.toon), plus [field-contract discovery PR #40](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ado/pull/40). Do not rewrite these as a parallel generic sync framework.

**Work and acceptance.**
- Upstream backend-bound authoritative document/version reads, mutation preview, audit/history lookup, durable operation identity/intents and lease/revision fencing; consume them here without deriving storage paths.
- Retain Azure `System.Rev` and JSON Patch `/rev` assertion, organization/project identity, field constraints, typed relation provenance and reviewed decisions. Capability mapping must distinguish provider authority from a projection or sync bridge.
- Preserve the distributed failure model: a local SQL transaction cannot atomically commit a remote REST PATCH. Durable prepared/applied/reconciled receipts and retry identities must survive ambiguous remote success, local commit failure, lease loss and process interruption. Avoid holding a database transaction indefinitely across network I/O; any changed sequencing must preserve existing reviewed-version checks.
- Backend conformance covers filesystem plus a native database without a local tracker: two competing local writers; stale Azure revision; replay after remote success/local failure; history-based settlement; missing/unsupported capability refusal; relation round-trip fidelity; authorization boundaries. Use synthetic REST responses, no live provider writes.
- Reuse existing resolution fixtures and prove they retain their failure sensitivity. Report unsupported remote capabilities honestly; generic SDK semantics must not silently flatten provider-native types.

**Investigation limits:** exact source revisions cited above were inspected read-only on 2026-10-25. No runtime tests or provider operations were performed for this proposal. All-status GitHub issues/PRs and relevant canonical project records were checked for overlap.

**Coordinated upstream dependencies:** [ports and coupling inventory #1587](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1587), [backend conformance #1588](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1588), and [migration fidelity #1589](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1589). See the [coordinated roadmap](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1399#issuecomment-6400102270). Contribute this package's native-provider and consumer requirements to those contracts early; these are upstream implementation dependencies, not a reason to defer surfacing constraints until the interfaces are finished.
Backend roadmap: preserve revision-bound reconciliation and recovery across native backends
